description: Placement-focused MCQs covering HTML, CSS, JavaScript, accessibility, responsive design, React, performance, browser APIs, tooling, testing, and frontend security.

questions.question: Which HTML element represents the main content of a document?

options.A: <header>

questions.explanation: The main element identifies the dominant content of the document body.

questions.question: Which attribute provides alternative text for an informative image?

options.A: title

questions.explanation: The alt attribute provides a text alternative for an image.

questions.question: Which element is most appropriate for a self-contained composition such as a blog post?

options.A: <article>

questions.explanation: The article element represents a self-contained composition that could be distributed independently.

questions.question: Which element associates a text caption with a form control?

options.A: <label>

questions.explanation: A label can be associated with a form control using for and id or by nesting the control.

questions.question: Which attribute on a script element is commonly used to defer execution until after HTML parsing?

options.A: defer

questions.explanation: For classic external scripts, defer delays execution until parsing completes and preserves document order.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the HTML lang attribute on the html element?

options.A: Set the document's primary language

questions.explanation: The lang attribute helps browsers and assistive technologies identify the document language.

questions.question: Which input type is designed for email addresses and provides built-in format validation in supporting browsers?

options.A: text

questions.explanation: The email input type offers browser-level email-format validation.

questions.question: Which element is intended to contain navigation links?

options.A: <nav>

questions.explanation: The nav element represents a section of navigation links.

questions.question: Why should a page generally have a clear heading hierarchy?

options.A: It improves document structure and navigation for users and assistive technologies
options.B: It guarantees a higher search ranking

questions.explanation: Headings communicate the document outline and help users navigate content.

questions.question: Which attribute makes a form control mandatory before a supported native form submission?

options.A: required

questions.explanation: The required attribute triggers browser validation that the control has a value.

questions.question: Which CSS property changes the text color?

options.A: font-style

questions.explanation: The color property sets the foreground color of text.

questions.question: Which selector targets elements with class name card?

options.A: #card

questions.explanation: A dot selector targets elements with the specified class.

questions.question: Which CSS layout system is particularly useful for arranging items in one dimension?

options.A: Flexbox

questions.explanation: Flexbox is designed for one-dimensional layout along a row or column.

questions.question: Which CSS unit is relative to the root element's font size?

options.A: px

questions.explanation: rem is relative to the computed font size of the root element.

questions.question: Which property controls the space inside an element's border?

options.A: margin

questions.explanation: Padding is the space between an element's content and its border.

questions.question: Which CSS property helps control what happens when content exceeds an element's box?

options.A: overflow

questions.explanation: The overflow property controls clipping or scrolling of overflowing content.

questions.question: In the standard CSS box model, what does box-sizing: border-box do?

options.A: Includes padding and border in the declared width and height

questions.explanation: With border-box, declared width and height include content, padding, and border.

questions.question: Which pseudo-class selects an element while the pointer is over it?

options.A: :focus

questions.explanation: The :hover pseudo-class matches an element while the pointing device hovers over it.

questions.question: Which selector generally has the highest specificity among these options?

options.A: .menu a

questions.explanation: An ID selector contributes more specificity than class, pseudo-class, or type selectors.

questions.question: Which at-rule is commonly used to apply responsive styles based on viewport width?

options.A: @font-face

questions.explanation: Media queries conditionally apply styles based on media features such as viewport width.

questions.question: Which keyword declares a block-scoped variable that can be reassigned?

options.A: const

questions.explanation: let declares a block-scoped binding that can be reassigned.

questions.question: Which operator checks strict equality without type coercion?
questions.explanation: Strict equality compares values without converting their types.

questions.question: Which method adds an item to the end of an array?

options.A: push()

questions.explanation: push appends one or more elements and returns the new array length.

questions.question: What does Array.prototype.map() return?

options.A: A new array containing callback results
options.B: The original array sorted in place

questions.explanation: map creates a new array from the callback result for each element.

questions.question: What does Array.prototype.filter() do?

options.A: Creates a new array containing elements that pass a test

questions.explanation: filter returns a new array with elements whose callback result is truthy.

questions.question: What does a Promise represent?

options.A: The eventual completion or failure of an asynchronous operation

questions.explanation: A Promise represents a future fulfilled value or rejection reason.

questions.question: Which syntax is used to handle a rejected promise in a try/catch with await?

options.A: await inside an async function with try/catch

questions.explanation: Awaited promise rejections can be handled with try/catch in an async function.

questions.question: What does event bubbling mean?

options.A: An event propagates from a target through ancestor elements
options.C: A listener runs before the target in every phase

questions.explanation: Bubbling propagates an event from the target toward its ancestors.

questions.question: What is a closure?

options.A: A function together with access to its surrounding lexical environment

questions.explanation: A closure retains access to variables from its lexical scope.

questions.question: What is the purpose of addEventListener()?

options.A: Register a callback for a specified event on a target

questions.explanation: addEventListener registers a function to be called when the specified event occurs.

questions.question: Which method selects the first element matching a CSS selector?

options.A: getElementsByTagName()

questions.explanation: querySelector returns the first matching element or null.

questions.question: Which property is generally safer than assigning untrusted text to innerHTML when only plain text is needed?

options.A: textContent

questions.explanation: textContent treats the value as text rather than parsing it as HTML.

questions.question: What does event.preventDefault() do?

options.A: Cancels the browser's default action for a cancelable event

questions.explanation: preventDefault cancels the default action but does not itself stop propagation.

questions.question: What does event.stopPropagation() do?

options.A: Stops the event from propagating further through the event path

questions.explanation: stopPropagation prevents further propagation but does not automatically cancel default behavior.

questions.question: What should an accessible button provide?

options.A: A clear accessible name and keyboard operability
options.C: A click handler with no semantic role
options.D: A positive tabindex on every child

questions.explanation: Native buttons provide keyboard support and semantics; their purpose should be clearly named.

questions.question: Why should color not be the only way to communicate an error?

options.A: Some users may not perceive the color difference
options.D: Screen readers read all colors automatically

questions.explanation: Pairing color with text or symbols makes status information available to more users.

questions.question: Which attribute connects a form control to an explanatory element when appropriate?

options.A: aria-describedby

questions.explanation: aria-describedby references elements that provide additional descriptive text.

questions.question: What is a key advantage of semantic HTML over using generic div elements for everything?

options.A: Native meaning and behaviors improve accessibility and maintainability
options.C: It removes the need for CSS
options.D: It makes all pages load instantly

questions.explanation: Semantic elements expose meaningful roles and can provide useful built-in behavior.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the viewport meta tag on many mobile web pages?

options.A: Help the layout use the device viewport appropriately

questions.explanation: The viewport meta tag helps browsers size the layout viewport for mobile displays.

questions.question: Which approach is generally best for responsive page layouts?

options.A: Use flexible layouts and media queries where needed
options.C: Use images as the entire interface

questions.explanation: Flexible sizing and media queries adapt content to different viewports.

questions.question: What does mobile-first CSS generally mean?

options.A: Start with styles for smaller viewports and enhance for larger ones

questions.explanation: Mobile-first design starts with a small-screen baseline and adds enhancements for larger screens.

questions.question: Which resource hint can tell the browser to fetch a critical resource early?

options.A: preload

questions.explanation: preload can prioritize a resource needed soon by the current page.

questions.question: What is lazy loading for images?

options.A: Delay loading offscreen or noncritical images until needed
options.B: Compress every image to zero bytes
options.C: Load every image before HTML parsing

questions.explanation: Lazy loading can reduce initial network work by postponing noncritical image loads.

questions.question: What is a common benefit of minifying CSS and JavaScript?

options.A: Reducing file size by removing unnecessary characters
options.B: Making all code easier to debug in production

questions.explanation: Minification removes unnecessary characters and can reduce transfer size.

questions.question: What does code splitting commonly do in a frontend application?

options.A: Divide code into smaller chunks loaded when needed
options.B: Combine every file into one always-loaded bundle

questions.explanation: Code splitting can reduce initial bundle cost by loading some chunks on demand.

questions.question: Which function is used to create a React component with hooks in a common functional style?

options.A: A JavaScript function returning JSX

questions.explanation: A function component returns React elements, often expressed using JSX.

questions.question: What are props in React?

options.A: Inputs passed from a parent component to a child

questions.explanation: Props pass data and callbacks to a component.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the useState hook?

options.A: Store component state and provide a setter
options.B: Navigate directly to any URL securely

questions.explanation: useState lets a function component retain state between renders.

questions.question: Why should a list of React elements usually have a stable key?

options.A: Help React identify items across updates

questions.explanation: Keys help React match list items during reconciliation.

questions.question: What is the purpose of useEffect?

options.A: Synchronize a component with external systems after rendering

questions.explanation: useEffect is used for effects such as subscriptions, timers, and synchronization with external systems.

questions.question: Why should React state usually be updated immutably?

options.A: It helps React detect changes and avoids unintended shared mutations
options.B: It guarantees all updates are synchronous
options.C: It removes the need for keys
options.D: It makes every object frozen automatically

questions.explanation: Creating updated state values helps predictable rendering and avoids mutation bugs.

questions.question: What is a controlled input in React?

options.A: An input whose value is driven by React state
options.D: An input styled only with CSS

questions.explanation: A controlled input receives its value from state and updates through an event handler.

questions.question: What is JSX?

options.A: A syntax extension commonly used to describe UI elements in JavaScript

questions.explanation: JSX lets developers write markup-like syntax that is transformed into JavaScript calls.

questions.question: Why can using an array index as a key be problematic when list items are reordered?

options.A: The index may no longer identify the same logical item
options.D: It always causes a syntax error

questions.explanation: Index keys can cause state or DOM reuse to associate with the wrong item after reordering.

questions.question: Which browser API is commonly used to make HTTP requests from JavaScript?

options.A: fetch()

questions.explanation: fetch provides a promise-based interface for making network requests.

questions.question: What does localStorage generally provide?

options.A: Persistent string key-value storage for a browser origin
options.B: A relational database shared across every website

questions.explanation: localStorage stores string values by origin across browser sessions, but is not suitable for secrets.

questions.question: Why should a frontend application avoid storing long-lived sensitive tokens in localStorage when safer alternatives are available?

options.A: JavaScript-accessible storage can be exposed by XSS

questions.explanation: Scripts running in the origin can read localStorage, so XSS can expose stored tokens.

questions.question: What is CORS primarily used to control?

options.A: Whether browsers allow scripts from one origin to access resources from another origin

questions.explanation: CORS is a browser-enforced mechanism based on server response headers for cross-origin access.

questions.question: Why should a frontend not rely on client-side validation alone for security?

options.A: Users can bypass or alter client-side checks, so the server must validate too

questions.explanation: Client-side validation improves UX but server-side validation is required for trust boundaries.

questions.question: What is npm commonly used for in JavaScript projects?

options.A: Managing packages and running project scripts

questions.explanation: npm installs packages and runs scripts defined in package.json.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a bundler such as Vite or webpack in many frontend projects?

options.A: Transform and package frontend assets for development or production

questions.explanation: Bundlers and build tools process modules and assets for efficient development and deployment.

questions.question: What does ESLint help with?

options.A: Finding JavaScript code issues and enforcing lint rules

questions.explanation: ESLint analyzes JavaScript code against configured rules.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Git branches?

options.A: Develop changes in parallel without immediately changing the main line

questions.explanation: Branches isolate lines of development until changes are integrated.

questions.question: What is a unit test in frontend development?

options.A: A focused test of a small function or component behavior
options.B: A test of all internet routing

questions.explanation: Unit tests validate small pieces of logic or UI behavior.

questions.question: What is an end-to-end frontend test intended to verify?

options.A: A user workflow through the integrated application

questions.explanation: End-to-end tests exercise workflows in an integrated browser environment.

questions.question: What is a Content Security Policy (CSP) commonly used for?

options.A: Restrict sources from which certain page resources may load or execute

questions.explanation: CSP can reduce certain injection risks by restricting allowed resource sources.

questions.question: What is the critical rendering path?

options.A: The sequence of steps a browser uses to parse resources and render pixels

questions.explanation: The critical rendering path covers HTML/CSS processing, layout, and painting needed for rendering.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the browser's developer tools?

options.A: Inspect DOM, styles, network requests, performance, and runtime issues

questions.explanation: Developer tools help inspect and debug frontend behavior and performance.

questions.question: Which property controls the stacking order of positioned elements when stacking contexts apply?

options.A: z-index

questions.explanation: z-index controls stack level within the relevant stacking context.

questions.question: Which layout system is especially suited to two-dimensional rows and columns?

options.A: CSS Grid

questions.explanation: CSS Grid is designed for two-dimensional layout.

questions.question: What does position: fixed generally do?

options.A: Positions an element relative to the viewport, subject to containing-block rules
options.B: Places it in normal document flow only

questions.explanation: Fixed positioning normally anchors the element to the viewport, though certain ancestors can establish a containing block.

questions.question: What is a stacking context?

options.A: A local hierarchy for compositing elements along the z-axis

questions.explanation: A stacking context groups elements for z-order painting independently of other contexts.

questions.question: Which attribute associates a label with a form input by ID?

options.A: for

questions.explanation: The label's for value should match the input's id.

questions.question: Which element is intended to provide a disclosure widget that users can open and close?

options.A: <details>

questions.explanation: The details element creates a disclosure widget, typically with a summary child.

questions.question: What is the result of typeof null in JavaScript?

options.A: "null"

questions.explanation: For historical reasons, typeof null returns the string object.

questions.question: What does Promise.all() do if one of its input promises rejects?

options.A: Rejects as soon as a rejection is observed
options.B: Always waits for every promise and returns all values

questions.explanation: Promise.all rejects when an input promise rejects; it does not automatically retry.

questions.question: Which operator provides a default only when the left side is null or undefined?
questions.explanation: The nullish coalescing operator uses the right operand only for null or undefined.

questions.question: What is event delegation?

options.A: Handling events on an ancestor for matching descendant events
options.B: Registering a separate global listener for every event forever

questions.explanation: Event delegation uses event propagation to handle events from descendants at a common ancestor.

questions.question: Why should side effects not generally be performed directly during React render?

options.A: Rendering should remain pure so React can safely render or retry
options.D: Side effects only work in CSS

questions.explanation: Pure rendering avoids unexpected effects when React renders more than once or abandons a render.

questions.question: What is a common use of React Context?

options.A: Share values across a component subtree without passing props through every level

questions.explanation: Context shares values such as theme or authenticated-user state across descendants.

questions.question: What does keyboard accessibility require for interactive controls?

options.A: Users can operate them without relying on a pointer
options.C: All controls must be div elements

questions.explanation: Interactive controls should be reachable and operable by keyboard with visible focus.

questions.question: What is cumulative layout shift (CLS) concerned with?

options.A: Unexpected movement of visible page content during loading or use

questions.explanation: CLS measures unexpected visual instability caused by layout shifts.

questions.question: Why specify image width and height or an aspect ratio?

options.A: Reserve layout space and reduce unexpected shifts
options.D: Remove the need for alt text

questions.explanation: Known dimensions let browsers reserve space before image content loads.

questions.question: What does AbortController commonly help with in frontend JavaScript?

options.A: Cancel supported operations such as fetch requests

questions.explanation: An AbortSignal can cancel supported asynchronous operations such as fetch.

questions.question: What is the Same-Origin Policy intended to restrict?

options.A: Certain interactions between documents and resources from different origins
options.D: All HTTP requests regardless of origin

questions.explanation: The policy isolates origins and limits script access across origins.

questions.question: What is a lockfile such as package-lock.json used for?

options.A: Record a resolved dependency tree for more reproducible installs

questions.explanation: A lockfile records resolved package versions and dependency relationships.

questions.question: Why are visual regression tests useful?

options.A: Detect unintended changes to rendered appearance

questions.explanation: Visual regression tests compare rendered output to detect unexpected appearance changes.

questions.question: Which property defines how a flex container distributes items along its main axis?

options.A: justify-content

questions.explanation: justify-content aligns flex items along the main axis.

questions.question: Which property aligns flex items along the cross axis in a single flex line?

options.A: align-items

questions.explanation: align-items controls cross-axis alignment for flex items.

questions.question: Which element creates a hyperlink to another resource?
questions.explanation: The anchor element creates hyperlinks using href.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the button type attribute in a form?

options.A: Specify whether the button submits, resets, or acts as a regular button

questions.explanation: The type attribute determines button behavior, such as submit, reset, or button.

questions.question: What does JSON.parse() do?

options.A: Parse a JSON-formatted string into a JavaScript value
options.B: Convert any value to a JSON string

questions.explanation: JSON.parse parses valid JSON text into a JavaScript value.

questions.question: What does JSON.stringify() do?

options.A: Serialize a JavaScript value into JSON text where supported
options.B: Parse JSON text into an object

questions.explanation: JSON.stringify converts supported JavaScript values into a JSON string.

questions.question: What is lifting state up in React?

options.A: Moving shared state to the closest common ancestor that needs to coordinate it

questions.explanation: Lifting state up allows sibling components to share a single source of truth.

questions.question: What does a React fragment allow?

options.A: Group children without adding an extra DOM element
options.C: Persist state after a page reload

questions.explanation: Fragments group elements without introducing an extra DOM node.

questions.question: What does the CSS function minmax() commonly do in Grid?

options.A: Set a minimum and maximum size range for a track

questions.explanation: minmax specifies a track size range for CSS Grid.

questions.question: What is requestAnimationFrame commonly used for?

options.A: Schedule work before the browser's next repaint

questions.explanation: requestAnimationFrame schedules a callback before a repaint, useful for animation updates.

questions.question: What is the DOM?

options.A: A tree-like object representation of a document that scripts can inspect and modify

questions.explanation: The DOM represents document structure as objects that scripts can access and update.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the rel="noopener" attribute on a link opened in a new browsing context?

options.A: Prevent the opened page from accessing the opener reference in supported cases

questions.explanation: noopener prevents the new browsing context from receiving a usable window.opener reference.

questions.question: What does a visible focus indicator help users identify?

options.A: Which interactive element currently has keyboard focus
options.B: Which element has the highest z-index

questions.explanation: Visible focus indicators help keyboard users track their location.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: which element represents a thematic standalone section of content?

options.A: <section>

questions.explanation: The section element groups thematically related content, typically with a heading.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: which property changes the space outside an element's border?

options.A: padding

questions.explanation: Margin creates space outside the border.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: what is the difference between let and const?

options.A: let can be reassigned; const binding cannot be reassigned
options.D: They are identical in every way

questions.explanation: Both are block-scoped; const prevents reassignment of the binding, not mutation of referenced objects.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: which method creates a new element node?

options.A: document.createElement()

questions.explanation: createElement creates an element node that can later be inserted into the DOM.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: what does WCAG contrast guidance help ensure?

options.A: Text and UI components are distinguishable against their backgrounds

questions.explanation: Sufficient contrast helps users perceive text and interface components.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: what is a media query used for?

options.A: Apply CSS conditionally based on media features

questions.explanation: Media queries apply CSS based on features such as viewport size or user preferences.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: what is Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) intended to measure?

options.A: When the largest relevant content element becomes visible

questions.explanation: LCP measures the render time of the largest contentful element in the viewport.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: what does React reconciliation do?

options.A: Compare rendered element descriptions and update the DOM as needed

questions.explanation: Reconciliation determines the updates needed to bring the UI in line with the rendered tree.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: what does HTTP status 200 usually indicate?

options.A: The request succeeded

questions.explanation: 200 OK indicates that the request succeeded.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: where are npm scripts commonly defined?

options.A: package.json

questions.explanation: The scripts field in package.json defines commands run with npm run.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: what is a common defense against clickjacking?

options.A: Use suitable frame-ancestors CSP or X-Frame-Options policy
options.D: Set every link to target blank

questions.explanation: Frame restrictions can prevent unauthorized embedding of sensitive pages.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: which tool can inspect network requests made by a frontend page?

options.A: Browser developer tools Network panel

questions.explanation: The Network panel shows requests, responses, timing, and related details.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: which attribute opens a link in a new browsing context?

options.A: target="_blank"

questions.explanation: target="_blank" requests a new browsing context; security and relationship attributes should also be considered.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: which property controls whether an element is displayed as a flex container?

options.A: display: flex

questions.explanation: display:flex establishes a flex formatting context for the element's children.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: what does Array.prototype.reduce() commonly do?

options.A: Accumulates array elements into a single result

questions.explanation: reduce applies a callback to accumulate a result across array elements.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: which method removes an element from the DOM?

options.A: element.remove()

questions.explanation: The remove method removes the element from its parent.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: what should an accessible icon-only button have?

options.A: An accessible name describing its action
options.D: A title attribute in every possible case and nothing else

questions.explanation: Icon-only controls need a programmatic accessible name, often through text or aria-label.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: which CSS unit is based on the viewport width?

options.A: vw

questions.explanation: 1vw is one percent of the viewport width.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: what is Interaction to Next Paint (INP) concerned with?

options.A: Responsiveness of interactions across a page visit

questions.explanation: INP assesses interaction responsiveness by observing interaction-to-paint delays.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: why should state updates based on previous state use a functional updater when appropriate?

options.A: It avoids relying on a possibly stale captured state value

questions.explanation: Functional updaters receive the latest queued state value.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: what does HTTP status 301 generally indicate?

options.A: A permanent redirect

questions.explanation: 301 indicates a permanent redirect to another URI.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: what is a source map used for?

options.A: Map transformed or minified code back to original source during debugging

questions.explanation: Source maps help developer tools associate generated code with original sources.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: why is client-side role checking insufficient to secure an API?

options.A: A user can modify frontend code or call the API directly

questions.explanation: Authorization must be enforced by the trusted server for each protected operation.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: what is a useful first step when a UI bug occurs only at a certain viewport size?

options.A: Reproduce it at that size and inspect layout styles and computed dimensions

questions.explanation: Reproduction and inspection isolate the responsive layout cause.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: what does the autocomplete attribute help control?

options.A: Browser suggestions or autofill behavior for form fields

questions.explanation: autocomplete gives the browser hints about whether and how to autofill form controls.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: which property can make an image cover a fixed-size box while preserving its aspect ratio?

options.A: object-fit: cover

questions.explanation: object-fit:cover scales replaced content to fill its box, cropping excess if needed.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: which value is falsy in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: Numeric zero is falsy; arrays, objects, and nonempty strings are truthy.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: what does event.target usually refer to?

options.A: The original target of the event

questions.explanation: event.target is the object on which the event was dispatched, even while it bubbles.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: why is a skip link useful?

options.A: It lets keyboard users bypass repeated navigation to reach main content

questions.explanation: Skip links reduce repeated keyboard navigation through common page regions.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: what is the main benefit of a fluid layout?

options.A: Dimensions can adapt to available space
options.B: Every element has a fixed pixel width

questions.explanation: Fluid sizing helps layouts adapt to different viewport dimensions.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: why can large JavaScript bundles hurt user experience?

options.A: They can increase download, parse, compile, and execution costs

questions.explanation: Large bundles can delay interactivity, particularly on slower devices and connections.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: what is a common cause of an infinite render loop with useEffect?

options.A: An effect updates state in a way that changes a dependency on every render
options.B: A component has a CSS class

questions.explanation: An effect that repeatedly changes one of its dependencies can trigger repeated renders.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: what does HTTP status 401 generally mean?

options.A: Authentication is required or has failed

questions.explanation: 401 indicates missing or invalid authentication credentials in typical use.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: why separate development and production builds?

options.A: Development can favor diagnostics while production can optimize assets
options.C: Production builds must include every test tool
options.D: It removes the need for version control

questions.explanation: Different build modes support debugging during development and optimized delivery in production.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: what is a common XSS risk from rendering user content as HTML?

options.A: Untrusted content may execute script or inject markup
options.B: The page always loads more quickly

questions.explanation: Unsafe HTML insertion can turn attacker-controlled input into executable content.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: what is a regression test?

options.A: A test that checks existing behavior remains correct after changes
options.B: A test that checks only variable spelling

questions.explanation: Regression tests catch unintended changes to previously working behavior.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: which element provides a caption for a figure?

options.A: <figcaption>

questions.explanation: figcaption provides a caption or legend for its figure.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: which pseudo-element inserts generated content before an element's content?

options.A: ::before

questions.explanation: The ::before pseudo-element creates a generated box before the element's content.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: what does the spread syntax do with an iterable such as an array in an array literal?

options.A: Expands its elements into the new array

questions.explanation: Spread syntax expands iterable elements into the containing literal.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: what does event.currentTarget refer to while a listener runs?

options.A: The element whose listener is currently executing
options.D: The last child in the DOM

questions.explanation: currentTarget identifies the target to which the current listener is attached.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: which native HTML element should usually be preferred for an action that performs an operation?

options.A: button

questions.explanation: A button has built-in semantics and keyboard interaction for actions.

questions.question: During a frontend placement interview: what does the prefers-reduced-motion media feature help detect?

options.A: A user's preference for reduced nonessential motion
options.D: Whether the user is logged in

questions.explanation: The time element can use datetime to provide a machine-readable value.

questions.question: When optimizing a page for mobile devices: which value of position keeps an element in normal flow until a threshold, then sticks within its scroll container?

options.A: sticky

questions.explanation: position:sticky behaves like normal flow until its threshold and then sticks within its containing scroll context.

questions.question: When optimizing a page for mobile devices: what does optional chaining (?.) do?

options.A: Short-circuits property access when the preceding value is nullish
options.C: Converts a value to a string

questions.explanation: Optional chaining returns undefined rather than throwing when the checked base is null or undefined.

questions.question: When optimizing a page for mobile devices: what does focus() typically do when called on a focusable element?

options.A: Moves keyboard focus to that element
options.B: Scrolls to the page footer always

questions.explanation: focus() moves the document's focus to the element if it can be focused.

questions.question: When optimizing a page for mobile devices: why should modal dialogs manage focus carefully?

options.A: Users need to understand and operate the dialog and return to a sensible location afterward
options.B: Focus must always stay on the body

questions.explanation: Accessible modal dialogs manage initial focus, keyboard interaction, and focus restoration.

questions.question: When optimizing a page for mobile devices: what is the purpose of a CSS container query?

options.A: Style a component based on its container's size or features

questions.explanation: Container queries let components respond to their containing element's conditions.

questions.question: When optimizing a page for mobile devices: why should expensive work sometimes be moved to a Web Worker?

options.A: Keep CPU-heavy computation off the main UI thread
options.B: Give the worker direct DOM access

questions.explanation: Workers can perform computation away from the main thread, keeping the UI more responsive.

questions.question: When optimizing a page for mobile devices: why can an uncontrolled input be useful?

options.A: The DOM maintains its current value and React reads it when needed
options.D: It automatically saves to a database

questions.explanation: Uncontrolled inputs can be convenient when continuous React state synchronization is unnecessary.

questions.question: When optimizing a page for mobile devices: what is an idempotent HTTP method intended to mean?

options.A: Repeating the same request has the same intended effect on server state
options.B: It always returns the same response bytes
options.D: It must be a GET request

questions.explanation: Idempotency concerns the intended effect of repeated identical requests, not necessarily identical responses.

questions.question: When optimizing a page for mobile devices: what is semantic versioning commonly used for?

options.A: Communicate release changes and compatibility expectations

questions.explanation: Major, minor, and patch numbers communicate kinds of release changes.

questions.question: When optimizing a page for mobile devices: what is the safest general approach to handling secrets in a frontend app?

options.A: Keep secret credentials on the server and expose only limited public configuration

questions.explanation: Browser-delivered code and configuration can be inspected by users.

questions.question: When optimizing a page for mobile devices: what should be tested for a form with client-side validation?

options.A: Valid input, invalid input, boundary cases, and accessible error feedback

questions.explanation: Form tests should cover representative valid and invalid cases and how errors are communicated.

questions.question: When optimizing a page for mobile devices: which element associates a caption with a table?

options.A: <caption>

questions.explanation: The caption element supplies a title or description for a table.

questions.question: When optimizing a page for mobile devices: which CSS function can define responsive grid columns with a minimum track width?

options.A: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(...))

questions.explanation: repeat with auto-fit and minmax can create responsive grid tracks.

questions.question: When optimizing a page for mobile devices: what does Object.freeze() do at the top level?

options.A: Prevents changes to an object's own properties through ordinary operations

questions.explanation: Object.freeze is shallow and prevents ordinary changes to the object's own properties.

questions.question: When optimizing a page for mobile devices: which API is commonly used to observe whether an element enters or leaves a viewport or root intersection?

options.A: IntersectionObserver

questions.explanation: IntersectionObserver asynchronously reports intersection changes.

questions.question: When optimizing a page for mobile devices: what is the best way to indicate a required form field accessibly?

options.A: Use native required semantics and clear visible labeling or instructions

questions.explanation: Native required semantics plus clear instructions communicate the requirement to many users.

questions.question: When optimizing a page for mobile devices: which property creates space between items in modern flex and grid layouts?

options.A: gap

questions.explanation: gap sets spacing between rows and columns of layout items.

questions.question: When optimizing a page for mobile devices: what does code splitting by route often achieve?

options.A: Load route-specific code only when needed
options.C: Bundle all routes into every initial page

questions.explanation: Route-level splitting can reduce the initial JavaScript payload.

questions.question: When optimizing a page for mobile devices: what is the purpose of a router in a single-page application?

options.A: Map URLs and navigation to appropriate views
options.C: Replace the browser address bar entirely

questions.explanation: A router maps locations to views and manages client-side navigation.

questions.question: When optimizing a page for mobile devices: why should API error messages avoid exposing internal stack traces to users?

options.A: Stack traces may reveal implementation details and sensitive information

questions.explanation: Internal traces can expose paths, dependencies, and other details useful to attackers.

questions.question: When optimizing a page for mobile devices: why run a production build locally or in CI before deployment?

options.A: Catch build-time errors and verify deployable assets

questions.explanation: A production build validates that the project can produce its intended deployment artifacts.

questions.question: When optimizing a page for mobile devices: why is dependency vulnerability scanning useful?

options.A: It can identify known security advisories affecting installed packages

questions.explanation: Scanning can flag packages with known vulnerabilities for review and remediation.

questions.question: When optimizing a page for mobile devices: why should a failing test be investigated rather than automatically deleted?

options.A: It may reveal a real regression or an incorrect assumption
options.B: Tests cannot fail for valid reasons
options.D: A test failure always means the test is obsolete

questions.explanation: A failure is evidence to investigate; the test or implementation may need correction.

questions.question: In a React-based project: which element represents a thematic standalone section of content?

options.A: <section>

questions.explanation: The section element groups thematically related content, typically with a heading.

questions.question: In a React-based project: which property changes the space outside an element's border?

options.A: padding

questions.explanation: Margin creates space outside the border.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what is the difference between let and const?

options.A: let can be reassigned; const binding cannot be reassigned
options.D: They are identical in every way

questions.explanation: Both are block-scoped; const prevents reassignment of the binding, not mutation of referenced objects.

questions.question: In a React-based project: which method creates a new element node?

options.A: document.createElement()

questions.explanation: createElement creates an element node that can later be inserted into the DOM.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what does WCAG contrast guidance help ensure?

options.A: Text and UI components are distinguishable against their backgrounds

questions.explanation: Sufficient contrast helps users perceive text and interface components.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what is a media query used for?

options.A: Apply CSS conditionally based on media features

questions.explanation: Media queries apply CSS based on features such as viewport size or user preferences.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what is Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) intended to measure?

options.A: When the largest relevant content element becomes visible

questions.explanation: LCP measures the render time of the largest contentful element in the viewport.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what does React reconciliation do?

options.A: Compare rendered element descriptions and update the DOM as needed

questions.explanation: Reconciliation determines the updates needed to bring the UI in line with the rendered tree.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what does HTTP status 200 usually indicate?

options.A: The request succeeded

questions.explanation: 200 OK indicates that the request succeeded.

questions.question: In a React-based project: where are npm scripts commonly defined?

options.A: package.json

questions.explanation: The scripts field in package.json defines commands run with npm run.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what is a common defense against clickjacking?

options.A: Use suitable frame-ancestors CSP or X-Frame-Options policy
options.D: Set every link to target blank

questions.explanation: Frame restrictions can prevent unauthorized embedding of sensitive pages.

questions.question: In a React-based project: which tool can inspect network requests made by a frontend page?

options.A: Browser developer tools Network panel

questions.explanation: The Network panel shows requests, responses, timing, and related details.

questions.question: In a React-based project: which attribute opens a link in a new browsing context?

options.A: target="_blank"

questions.explanation: target="_blank" requests a new browsing context; security and relationship attributes should also be considered.

questions.question: In a React-based project: which property controls whether an element is displayed as a flex container?

options.A: display: flex

questions.explanation: display:flex establishes a flex formatting context for the element's children.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what does Array.prototype.reduce() commonly do?

options.A: Accumulates array elements into a single result

questions.explanation: reduce applies a callback to accumulate a result across array elements.

questions.question: In a React-based project: which method removes an element from the DOM?

options.A: element.remove()

questions.explanation: The remove method removes the element from its parent.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what should an accessible icon-only button have?

options.A: An accessible name describing its action
options.D: A title attribute in every possible case and nothing else

questions.explanation: Icon-only controls need a programmatic accessible name, often through text or aria-label.

questions.question: In a React-based project: which CSS unit is based on the viewport width?

options.A: vw

questions.explanation: 1vw is one percent of the viewport width.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what is Interaction to Next Paint (INP) concerned with?

options.A: Responsiveness of interactions across a page visit

questions.explanation: INP assesses interaction responsiveness by observing interaction-to-paint delays.

questions.question: In a React-based project: why should state updates based on previous state use a functional updater when appropriate?

options.A: It avoids relying on a possibly stale captured state value

questions.explanation: Functional updaters receive the latest queued state value.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what does HTTP status 301 generally indicate?

options.A: A permanent redirect

questions.explanation: 301 indicates a permanent redirect to another URI.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what is a source map used for?

options.A: Map transformed or minified code back to original source during debugging

questions.explanation: Source maps help developer tools associate generated code with original sources.

questions.question: In a React-based project: why is client-side role checking insufficient to secure an API?

options.A: A user can modify frontend code or call the API directly

questions.explanation: Authorization must be enforced by the trusted server for each protected operation.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what is a useful first step when a UI bug occurs only at a certain viewport size?

options.A: Reproduce it at that size and inspect layout styles and computed dimensions

questions.explanation: Reproduction and inspection isolate the responsive layout cause.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what does the autocomplete attribute help control?

options.A: Browser suggestions or autofill behavior for form fields

questions.explanation: autocomplete gives the browser hints about whether and how to autofill form controls.

questions.question: In a React-based project: which property can make an image cover a fixed-size box while preserving its aspect ratio?

options.A: object-fit: cover

questions.explanation: object-fit:cover scales replaced content to fill its box, cropping excess if needed.

questions.question: In a React-based project: which value is falsy in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: Numeric zero is falsy; arrays, objects, and nonempty strings are truthy.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what does event.target usually refer to?

options.A: The original target of the event

questions.explanation: event.target is the object on which the event was dispatched, even while it bubbles.

questions.question: In a React-based project: why is a skip link useful?

options.A: It lets keyboard users bypass repeated navigation to reach main content

questions.explanation: Skip links reduce repeated keyboard navigation through common page regions.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what is the main benefit of a fluid layout?

options.A: Dimensions can adapt to available space
options.B: Every element has a fixed pixel width

questions.explanation: Fluid sizing helps layouts adapt to different viewport dimensions.

questions.question: In a React-based project: why can large JavaScript bundles hurt user experience?

options.A: They can increase download, parse, compile, and execution costs

questions.explanation: Large bundles can delay interactivity, particularly on slower devices and connections.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what is a common cause of an infinite render loop with useEffect?

options.A: An effect updates state in a way that changes a dependency on every render
options.B: A component has a CSS class

questions.explanation: An effect that repeatedly changes one of its dependencies can trigger repeated renders.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what does HTTP status 401 generally mean?

options.A: Authentication is required or has failed

questions.explanation: 401 indicates missing or invalid authentication credentials in typical use.

questions.question: In a React-based project: why separate development and production builds?

options.A: Development can favor diagnostics while production can optimize assets
options.C: Production builds must include every test tool
options.D: It removes the need for version control

questions.explanation: Different build modes support debugging during development and optimized delivery in production.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what is a common XSS risk from rendering user content as HTML?

options.A: Untrusted content may execute script or inject markup
options.B: The page always loads more quickly

questions.explanation: Unsafe HTML insertion can turn attacker-controlled input into executable content.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what is a regression test?

options.A: A test that checks existing behavior remains correct after changes
options.B: A test that checks only variable spelling

questions.explanation: Regression tests catch unintended changes to previously working behavior.

questions.question: In a React-based project: which element provides a caption for a figure?

options.A: <figcaption>

questions.explanation: figcaption provides a caption or legend for its figure.

questions.question: In a React-based project: which pseudo-element inserts generated content before an element's content?

options.A: ::before

questions.explanation: The ::before pseudo-element creates a generated box before the element's content.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what does the spread syntax do with an iterable such as an array in an array literal?

options.A: Expands its elements into the new array

questions.explanation: Spread syntax expands iterable elements into the containing literal.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what does event.currentTarget refer to while a listener runs?

options.A: The element whose listener is currently executing
options.D: The last child in the DOM

questions.explanation: currentTarget identifies the target to which the current listener is attached.

questions.question: In a React-based project: which native HTML element should usually be preferred for an action that performs an operation?

options.A: button

questions.explanation: A button has built-in semantics and keyboard interaction for actions.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what does the prefers-reduced-motion media feature help detect?

options.A: A user's preference for reduced nonessential motion
options.D: Whether the user is logged in

questions.explanation: prefers-reduced-motion lets sites adapt animations to user preferences.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what does tree shaking attempt to remove?

options.A: Unused code from a bundle when static analysis allows it

questions.explanation: Tree shaking removes unused exports or code where the module structure allows it.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what is the purpose of React.memo?

options.A: Memoize a component render when props compare equal under its configured comparison
options.C: Make effects run on every event

questions.explanation: React.memo can skip rendering when props have not changed according to its comparison.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what does HTTP status 403 generally indicate?

options.A: The server understood the request but refuses to authorize it

questions.explanation: 403 indicates the server refuses to fulfill the request, often due to authorization.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what does a package manager lockfile help stabilize?

options.A: Resolved dependency versions across installations

questions.explanation: Lockfiles preserve the dependency resolution for repeatable installs.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what does CSRF attempt to exploit?

options.A: A browser's authenticated state to make an unwanted request

questions.explanation: CSRF tricks a user's browser into sending an authenticated action to a site.

questions.question: In a React-based project: why mock an API in a component test?

options.A: Control responses and test loading, success, and error states predictably

questions.explanation: Mocked responses make component behavior easier to test deterministically.

questions.question: In a React-based project: which attribute can specify multiple image sources for different viewport sizes?

options.A: srcset

questions.explanation: srcset lets browsers choose among image candidates based on resolution or conditions.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what does inherit do as a CSS value?

options.A: Uses the parent's computed value for that property
options.B: Resets the property to the browser default

questions.explanation: inherit explicitly takes the computed value from the parent.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what is the purpose of a JavaScript module export?

options.A: Make selected bindings available to importing modules

questions.explanation: Exports expose bindings for other modules to import.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what is a benefit of event delegation?

options.A: It can handle events for many descendants with fewer listeners
options.D: It removes the need for semantic HTML

questions.explanation: Delegation uses bubbling to handle descendant events at an ancestor.

questions.question: In a React-based project: which native element should usually be used for navigation to another URL?

options.A: a with href

questions.explanation: An anchor with href provides native link semantics and keyboard behavior.

questions.question: In a React-based project: which technique can prevent long text from forcing a flex child wider than expected?

options.A: min-width: 0 on the flex item where appropriate
options.B: Set every parent to position: fixed

questions.explanation: Flex items may have an automatic minimum size; min-width:0 can allow shrinking.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what is a common reason to avoid synchronous layout reads mixed with repeated style writes?

options.A: They can trigger forced layout and cause layout thrashing

questions.explanation: Alternating layout reads and writes can force repeated expensive layout calculations.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what does a React error boundary generally catch?

options.A: Errors thrown while rendering descendants and certain lifecycle work

questions.explanation: Error boundaries catch certain descendant render and lifecycle errors, not every asynchronous or event-handler error.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what does the Cache-Control header help specify?

options.A: Caching directives for HTTP responses or requests

questions.explanation: Cache-Control communicates caching policies such as max-age and no-store.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what is a linter different from a formatter in general?

options.A: A linter flags code patterns or potential issues; a formatter standardizes layout

questions.explanation: Linters analyze code against rules; formatters consistently rewrite presentation.

questions.question: In a React-based project: which cookie attribute helps prevent JavaScript access to a cookie?

options.A: HttpOnly

questions.explanation: HttpOnly prevents access through document.cookie in browser JavaScript.

questions.question: In a React-based project: what is a flaky UI test commonly caused by?

options.A: Timing assumptions, animations, or unstable test data

questions.explanation: Flakiness often arises from race conditions, arbitrary sleeps, or non-isolated state.
